title: IBM and Together AI Sign $240 Million Deal for Nvidia-Powered AI Cluster
excerpt: The multi-year agreement will build a large-scale inference cluster on IBM Cloud using Nvidia's latest Blackwell processors to run open-source AI models at enterprise scale.
body:
• IBM and Together AI have agreed to a $240 million multi-year deal to build an AI inference cluster on IBM Cloud using Nvidia HGX B300 systems
  • The cluster will run open-source AI models as businesses increasingly seek cheaper alternatives to closed systems from OpenAI, Anthropic, and Meta
  • Together AI, led by Indian-origin CEO Vipul Ved Prakash, was valued at $8.3 billion in July after raising $800 million in Series C funding

IBM and AI startup Together AI have signed a $240 million multi-year agreement to build a large-scale artificial intelligence inference cluster on IBM Cloud using Nvidia systems, the companies announced on Tuesday.

The cluster will use Nvidia's HGX B300 systems, which link the chipmaker's newer Blackwell processors with its Spectrum-X Ethernet networking gear. Nvidia has said its Blackwell chips are optimized specifically for AI inference — the process of running trained models to generate responses, which has become one of the largest drivers of demand for computing capacity.

Open-Source AI Gains Ground

The deal underscores a broader industry shift toward open-source AI models, which have gained traction as businesses look to rein in costs and address cybersecurity concerns tied to proprietary models from Anthropic, OpenAI, and Meta, according to Reuters.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PMTHhjF78pw

San Francisco-based Together AI's platform enables companies to train and run AI workloads on open models such as DeepSeek, MiniMax, and Kimi at a fraction of the cost of closed systems. The company says its infrastructure delivers comparable or better performance while dramatically cutting inference expenses — one customer reported a sixfold reduction in costs after switching to the platform.

"Our mission is to ensure that intelligence is abundant, not expensive. The future of AI won't be owned by a few companies. It will be built by millions of developers and businesses, and open-source models are making that possible."

— Vipul Ved Prakash, Co-Founder and CEO, Together AI

Together AI's Rapid Rise

Together AI has grown rapidly since its founding in 2022. The company raised $800 million in a Series C round in July 2026, led by Aramco Ventures with participation from Vista Equity Partners, General Catalyst, Emergence Capital, and Nvidia, pushing its valuation to $8.3 billion — up from $3.3 billion in its February 2025 Series B.

Annual bookings topped $1.15 billion last quarter, and the company now serves thousands of paying customers. Alongside the equity capital, Together AI secured commitments for over 500 megawatts of compute capacity to support its expected growth.

The IBM deal represents a significant anchor customer arrangement and marks Together AI's expansion beyond its own data centers into major enterprise cloud platforms.

Indian-Origin Leaders on Both Sides

The deal brings together two companies led by Indian-origin executives. Together AI's co-founder and CEO Vipul Ved Prakash grew up in New Delhi, attended St. Stephen's College, and previously founded social media search company Topsy Labs, which Apple acquired for over $200 million in 2013. MIT's Technology Review named him one of the world's top 100 young innovators in 2003.

On the other side, IBM is led by Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna, who has steered the 113-year-old technology giant toward AI and hybrid cloud since taking the helm in 2020. At GTC 2026 in March, Krishna emphasized the need for enterprises to move from AI experimentation to production at scale.

What's Next

The partnership comes as cloud providers and chipmakers spend billions of dollars expanding AI infrastructure to meet surging inference demand. IBM had already announced plans to offer Nvidia Blackwell Ultra GPUs on IBM Cloud starting in Q2 2026, and this deal with Together AI deepens that commitment with a dedicated inference cluster.

For the broader AI industry, the deal signals that open-source inference infrastructure is becoming a serious enterprise business. As model costs eat into margins for companies building AI-powered products, platforms like Together AI that offer cheaper alternatives to closed systems are positioned to capture a growing share of the market.
